courseReview.method: Read every selected course’s actual profile, legacy description, topics/methods, formal preq1 and every assigned term directly from current-main workbook. courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.contribution: Mandatory first-year formation; not a quantitative specialist or job-search replacement.

courses.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
courses.contribution: Specific complementary study of accounting information and financial statements helps interpret company data and economic events. The enriched content does not establish a full corporate-finance or quantitative-finance syllabus.

courses.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
courses.contribution: Specific complementary non-technical study of AI’s effects on business, labour markets, growth, governance and economic decisions supplies a defined application strand. It is not technical data-science training.

courses.name: Money, Banking & Finance
courses.contribution: Direct practical work with financial data, risk, investment, budgeting and business decisions supplies the financial-decision strand. It does not establish specialist econometric asset-pricing or banking-model training.

courses.name: Introduction to Economics
courses.contribution: provides the introductory microeconomic and macroeconomic framework needed for quantitative economic applications

courses.name: International Macroeconomics
courses.contribution: develops macroeconomic analysis of growth, inflation, policy, crises and international trade using economic data

courses.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
courses.contribution: develops advanced microeconomic analysis of uncertainty, strategic behaviour, market structure, equilibrium and efficiency

courses.name: Public Economics
courses.contribution: uses theoretical models and empirical evidence to analyse market failure, taxation, redistribution and public policy

courses.name: Econometrics
courses.contribution: directly develops econometric estimation, testing, causal analysis, prediction and Monte Carlo simulation in Stata

courses.name: Behavioral Economics
courses.contribution: develops evidence-based analysis of economic decision-making, biases and behavioural choice

courses.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
courses.contribution: Specific complementary venture study develops business-model and customer validation, market testing and business planning: concrete operating decisions underlying the business/financial strand. It also satisfies the formal prerequisite for Money, Banking & Finance; it is not counted as financial mathematics.

courses.name: Research Methods & Statistics
courses.contribution: provides foundational research design, statistics and empirical-analysis skills for later econometric work

courses.name: AI Ethics
courses.contribution: adds explicit ethical analysis of algorithmic systems, including fairness, accountability, privacy and responsibility

courses.name: Decision-making in AI
courses.contribution: develops computational decision models under uncertainty, partial observability, constraints and resource limits

courses.name: Logic & Discrete Mathematics
courses.contribution: provides discrete mathematics, logic and algorithmic structures useful for formal decision and optimisation problems

courses.name: Optimization Methods in AI
courses.contribution: develops search, constraint satisfaction and optimisation methods in discrete and continuous environments

courses.name: Reinforcement Learning
courses.contribution: develops algorithmic learning and sequential decision-making through reinforcement-learning models

courses.name: Database Management Systems
courses.contribution: Specific complementary data infrastructure: relational models, normalization, SQL and query processing support collection and preparation of economic/business datasets. This is not econometric inference.

courses.name: Software Development
courses.contribution: deepens programming and software-development practice in multiple languages for computational data work

courses.name: Algorithms & Data Structures
courses.contribution: develops algorithm design, data structures and performance analysis for computational modelling

courses.name: Advanced Algorithms
courses.contribution: develops advanced algorithms and computational solution methods for optimisation problems

courses.name: Introduction to Data Science
courses.contribution: develops foundational data cleaning, visualisation and analysis through applied research projects

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.contribution: develops predictive modelling through regression, classification, resampling, tree methods and clustering

courses.name: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
courses.contribution: Direct neural-network theory and Python/TensorFlow implementation, including tabular data, computer vision and text applications, extends the computational data-science route. These broader applications are not represented as additional econometrics training.

courses.name: Introduction to Programming
courses.contribution: provides the programming foundation in Python, computational problem-solving and basic discrete mathematics

courses.name: Mathematical Methods
courses.contribution: Direct foundation in differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations for mathematical modelling. Linear algebra is supplied separately by DISMATH211; the gateway outline is not credited with an eigenvalue syllabus.

courses.name: Linear Algebra
courses.contribution: develops matrix methods, vector spaces, linear transformations and systems of linear equations

courses.name: Computational & Numerical Methods
courses.contribution: Direct numerical treatment of equations, interpolation, differentiation, integration and ordinary differential equations, including accuracy and sensitivity. Its introductory mention of optimisation does not establish a specialist optimisation syllabus.

courses.name: Advanced Calculus
courses.contribution: extends calculus to multiple dimensions and differential equations for quantitative modelling

courses.name: Probability & Statistics
courses.contribution: develops probability theory, distributions, sampling, estimation and simulation as a mathematical-statistics foundation

courses.name: Ethics
courses.contribution: Specific complementary ethical theories and argumentation, including poverty, wealth, equality and responsibility, support evaluation of economic decisions. The course is not a substitute for profession-specific econometric ethics.

courses.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
courses.contribution: provides multivariate statistics, regression, factor analysis and related inference methods useful for complex empirical data
